headline: DPWH, MMDA Step Up Road Repairs After Monsoon Damage Ahead of Monday Traffic
seoTitle: DPWH, MMDA Step Up Monsoon Road Repairs | FMB News
seoDescription: DPWH and MMDA are accelerating repairs on monsoon-damaged roads ahead of heavier Monday traffic, according to the approved FMB News overnight brief.
deck: Road crews are accelerating patching and restoration work after days of heavy rain, with priority placed on heavily used corridors before Monday's commuter surge.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Public Works and Highways and the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority have intensified road-repair work following days of monsoon rain, according to the approved FMB News overnight brief.

The brief says crews are prioritizing pothole patching, damaged pavement and drainage-related road defects on heavily traveled corridors before Monday's expected return of heavier school and work traffic.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Prolonged rainfall can accelerate pavement deterioration when water enters cracks and weakened road layers. DPWH emergency-response rules also assign the department responsibility for clearing and restoring affected roads and other transport lifelines after disasters.

The approved brief identifies several specific corridors as priority areas. Because a same-day DPWH or MMDA release listing every corridor was not independently surfaced in search, FMB News is not presenting that route list as independently confirmed.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Damaged pavement creates safety risks for motorists and can worsen congestion when traffic volumes return to normal. Repairing drainage-related defects quickly also reduces the chance that another round of rain will enlarge potholes or undermine road surfaces.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch DPWH and MMDA advisories for lane closures, overnight repair windows, completed sections and any renewed damage if monsoon rains intensify again.
